subject: Biotechnology
title: Cells as Factories
description: A fast breakdown of Cells as Factories for builders.

hook.text: A single bacterial cell can produce a million copies of a human protein in hours — nature's factory.

buildup.text: Cells already have all the machinery — ribosomes, energy systems, quality control built in.

discovery.text: Biotechnologists insert new genetic instructions — the cell reads them and builds the desired product.

twist.text: Not all cells are equal — bacteria are fast but cannot fold complex human proteins correctly.

climax.text: Chinese hamster ovary cells make most antibody drugs — mammalian cells fold human proteins properly.

punchline.text: The best factories in biotech are alive — and microscopic.

quiz.question: Why are mammalian cells used instead of bacteria for some biotech products?
options: Bacteria grow too slowly to be useful
Mammalian cells can properly fold complex human proteins that bacteria cannot
Bacteria are too expensive to grow in large quantities

details.summary: Cells can be engineered into biological factories that produce valuable molecules from simple feedstocks. By inserting new genes or rewiring metabolic pathways, bacteria, yeast, or mammalian cells manufacture proteins, chemicals, and fuels that are difficult to make chemically.
details.whyItMatters: Cellular factories produce everything from insulin to biofuels using renewable inputs. This concept underpins the entire biomanufacturing industry and enables production of complex molecules that organic chemistry cannot efficiently synthesize.
takeaways: Cells are reprogrammed to produce specific proteins, chemicals, or fuels
Genetic engineering inserts production pathways into host organisms
Cellular manufacturing uses renewable feedstocks under mild conditions

faq.question: What types of cells are used as factories?
faq.answer: Bacteria like E. coli produce simple proteins and chemicals cheaply. Yeast handles more complex proteins and tolerates industrial conditions. Chinese hamster ovary cells produce therapeutic antibodies requiring mammalian modifications. The choice depends on product complexity.

faq.question: What advantages do cell factories have over chemical synthesis?
faq.answer: Cells operate at room temperature and neutral pH, use renewable sugars as feedstock, produce complex chiral molecules with perfect selectivity, and can be reprogrammed for new products by changing their DNA rather than redesigning chemical plants.
